$comment: What a clean run of the plugin should report. It is written by build.mjs from the same plan code the plugin runs, so comparing it against the receipt the plugin prints is a comparison of two numbers, not a reading of two documents. There is no date in this file on purpose: it is a pure function of the tokens, and the SHA-256 below changes only when they do.

decisions.what: No paint style was made for the 66 primitive ramp steps.
decisions.why: They exist as variables in the Primitives collection. A designer should reach for a role such as Theme/Ink/Default, which follows the theme, rather than for a fixed ramp step, which does not.

decisions.what: No elevation or shadow effect styles were made.
decisions.why: The token set has no shadow or elevation token. Inventing blur radii and opacities here would put numbers in the library that the system never agreed to.

decisions.what: Buttons are filled, and were outlined until 26 August 2026.
decisions.why: The reason they were outlined was that the semantic roles included no "on accent" text colour, so the label on a filled button was not defined anywhere in the system. That role now exists. color/accent/on is surface.lowest, measured as ink against every fill that carries it — accent, accent-hover and danger — with the worst of those published rather than the flattering one. So a filled button now uses only roles that were measured, which is what the outlined one was standing in for, and it matches what components.css ships.
The token set has no border-width token. 1 px is stated here rather than hidden in the drawing code.

decisions.what: Every badge carries a word, never colour alone.
decisions.why: In forced-colors mode all four status colours resolve to CanvasText, so a badge that carried only a colour would carry nothing. forced-colors.map.json states this as a rule.

knownGaps.what: Latin and monospaced text styles carry no line height.
knownGaps.why: The token set defines no line height at all. There was one, for Bangla, and it went with the Bangla. Figma’s automatic line height is used rather than a number I would have had to invent.
